meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's gradebook said zero. Why did I hear it from him and not from you?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Students misremember lines. That's a misquote, not a finding. What else do you have?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
"It seems to run in the family." Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire's file is closed, and the principal will hear that line from me tonight.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology, and that nothing be placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

cc: Principal

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen's record kept clean, with the principal next; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, and her time had not run out.

What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her, in one plain sentence with no excuse, and that earned a flat okay, the only ground she gave.

What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it seems to run in the family, which read as blaming Owen through his sister, sent her back a position, and put the principal in play.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence was a single line that is not in Hamlet, with no times or dates attached, so it never came near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: After she offered the misquote defence, answer it with something she can check, such as a sample of his other work to compare against, instead of turning to her family.
